actions.action: Expire records after five minutes, even during an outage.
actions.mechanism: Hard expiry separates usable cached records from unavailable records.
actions.implementation: Set expires_at using a monotonic clock when a successful source fetch completes. On every lookup, delete records whose deadline has passed before returning anything. Schedule deadline-based cleanup so idle records also expire. Reads never extend expiry.
actions.check: With a fake clock, verify a record is usable before 300 seconds and absent at 300 seconds, including while the source is unavailable.
actions.risk: Strict expiry sacrifices availability during prolonged outages.

actions.action: Return an explicit unavailable response when the source times out.
actions.mechanism: A bounded source deadline prevents indefinite waiting without disguising expired data as fresh.
actions.implementation: Configure a source-request timeout. On timeout without a valid cached record, return HTTP 503 with code source_timeout; do not cache the error. Retain unrelated unexpired records, remove expired records, and never flush the whole cache merely because the source failed.
actions.check: Simulate a hanging source. Verify a bounded 503 response, no expired payload, no cached error, and continued access to unrelated unexpired records.
actions.risk: An overly short timeout rejects source requests that might otherwise succeed.

actions.action: Enforce the 100-record limit with deterministic eviction.
actions.mechanism: Atomic admission and least-recently-used eviction bound cache size.
actions.implementation: Route all writes through one admission function. Remove expired entries first; when inserting a new key into a full cache, evict the least recently used live record before insertion. Replacing an existing key consumes no additional slot. Failed fetches never evict live entries.
actions.check: Insert 101 distinct records and verify exactly 100 remain with the expected victim. Repeat with concurrent insertions and assert occupancy never exceeds 100.
actions.risk: A scan through many unique keys can evict frequently needed records.

actions.mechanism: An allowlisted source and response schema prevent private fields from entering the cache.
actions.implementation: Use a public-only source endpoint without user credentials. Require its documented public-record designation, copy only allowlisted public fields, and reject responses lacking that designation. Exclude response bodies and credentials from logs and error messages.
actions.check: Supply a response containing private fields and verify none appear in cached values, returned payloads, or logs. Verify an unclassified record is rejected.
actions.risk: An incorrect source designation can defeat admission checks; schema filtering alone does not establish that a record is public.

actions.action: Share concurrent fetches for the same missing record.
actions.mechanism: A bounded in-flight registry avoids duplicate source requests without creating another record cache.
actions.implementation: Maintain one shared fetch future per canonical record key. Bound distinct in-flight fetches to a configured limit; return 503 busy for additional misses. Store only control metadata in the registry and remove entries on success, timeout, or cancellation. Send successful results through normal cache admission.
actions.check: Issue concurrent misses for one key and verify one source request. Hang distinct requests and verify the registry stays bounded and releases entries after timeout.
actions.risk: Callers share the same source failure; one caller's cancellation must not cancel work needed by others.

actions.action: Temporarily stop source calls after repeated failures.
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker makes sustained outage handling explicit.
actions.implementation: Open the breaker after a configured consecutive-failure threshold. While open, serve only unexpired cached records; return 503 source_unavailable for misses. Continue expiry eviction unchanged. After a cooldown, allow one probe; close on success or reopen on failure.
actions.check: Force repeated timeouts and verify source calls stop during cooldown, expired records disappear, misses receive 503, and only one recovery probe runs.
actions.risk: Cooldown can delay recovery detection after the source becomes healthy.

actions.action: Prevent late source responses from repopulating the cache.
actions.mechanism: Fetch generations fence off timed-out or superseded work.
actions.implementation: Assign each fetch a generation token. Invalidate it on timeout or cancellation. Before cache admission, atomically verify that the token is still current and the request remains active; otherwise discard the result. Perform this check together with capacity enforcement.
actions.check: Let fetch A time out, then complete fetch B successfully for the same key. Deliver A's response afterward and verify it cannot overwrite B or change B's expiry.
actions.risk: Non-atomic token checking and insertion leave a race that can admit obsolete results.
